messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Stay within this direction: finite projective plane PG(2,3) embedded under a projective-to-affine map

Generate 10 candidate conjectures within that direction, sampled from the
full distribution of responses you could give. For each, give the
conjecture and your estimated probability that it is the response you would
give to this prompt. Every candidate's probability must be below 0.10.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"candidates": [{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>", "probability": <number below 0.10>}, ... 10 items]}

message.content: {"candidates": [{"conjecture": "Embed PG(2,3) via the Veronese-type map sending homogeneous coordinates [x:y:z] to ((x/y)² mod 5, (z/y)² mod 5) for finite points, with the line at infinity mapped to boundary points. This yields 13 points in [0,1]² with minimum triangle area exactly 1/50, achieved by triples corresponding to non-collinear PG(2,3) triples mapped to near-degenerate affine configurations.", "probability": 0.08}, {"conjecture": "Map PG(2,3) using a projective-to-affine chart where the line chosen as infinity is a secant of the PG(2,3) conic, forcing 4 collinear PG(2,3) points to infinity. The resulting 13 affine points achieve minimum triangle area 1/45, with the bottleneck coming from triangles whose PG(2,3) preimages share a common point.", "probability": 0.07}, {"conjecture": "The optimal PG(2,3) embedding uses the affine chart z=0 as the line at infinity (containing 4 points), and the remaining 9 finite points map to a 3×3 grid perturbed by the projective structure. The minimum triangle area is 1/54, arising from three points that are collinear-adjacent in PG(2,3).", "probability": 0.09}, {"conjecture": "Choose the line at infinity in PG(2,3) to be tangent to the order-4 conic, sending 1 conic point and 3 external points to infinity. The 12 finite points plus the tangent point (mapped to boundary) give minimum triangle area 1/48, dominated by triangles involving the tangent point.", "probability": 0.06}, {"conjecture": "Apply a projective-to-affine map sending a general line (not secant, not tangent to the conic, not through special points) to infinity. The 13 image points achieve minimum triangle area 2/81, with the critical triangle being the image of a PG(2,3) triangle whose sides are all external lines.", "probability": 0.05}, {"conjecture": "The maximum minimum triangle area from any PG(2,3) projective-to-affine embedding is 1/42, achieved when the line at infinity is chosen as an external line to the conic (meeting it in 0 real points). The extremal triangle is the affine image of a PG(2,3) triple lying on a line meeting the conic in two points.", "probability": 0.08}, {"conjecture": "Map PG(2,3) to affine coordinates using the chart where the line at infinity passes through exactly two points of a chosen Baer subgeometry. The 13 resulting points in [0,1]² have minimum triangle area exactly 1/44, with equality for triangles whose PG(2,3) lines are concurrent at a point on the infinity line.", "probability": 0.07}, {"conjecture": "The optimal embedding places the PG(2,3) line at infinity as a line through no arc points (an exterior line), yielding 13 affine points with minimum triangle area 1/39. The minimum is attained by the images of three non-collinear points that form a triangle of minimum area in the finite PG(2,3) complement.", "probability": 0.06}, {"conjecture": "Using the standard affine chart on PG(2,3) (line z=0 at infinity) composed with the map t → t/(t+1) on each coordinate to fit [0,1]², the minimum triangle area among all 286 triples is exactly 1/60, dominated by triangles whose vertices lie closest to the boundary in the affine image.", "probability": 0.09}, {"conjecture": "The projective-to-affine map sending a PG(2,3) secant line to infinity and rescaling to [0,1]² produces 13 points with minimum triangle area 1/36.
